english: Let $R=\left\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}:|x|+|y|\le 4\le |x|+|y|+|xy|\right\}$. Then the area of $R$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $R=\left\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}:|x|+|y|\le 4\le |x|+|y|+|xy|\right\}$ है। तब $R$ का क्षेत्रफल ______ है।
solution: Only $|x|,|y|$ appear, so $R$ is symmetric about both axes: area $=4\times$ first-quadrant part.
solution_full: Each condition involves only $|x|$, $|y|$ and $|xy|=|x||y|$, so $R$ is symmetric about both axes and its area is four times the area of $R\cap\{x\ge 0,y\ge 0\}$.
In the first quadrant: $x+y\le 4$ (inside the square $|x|+|y|=4$) and $x+y+xy\ge 4$. Adding 1: $1+x+y+xy\ge 5$, i.e. $(1+x)(1+y)\ge 5$, so $y\ge\dfrac{5}{1+x}-1=\dfrac{4-x}{1+x}$.

For $0\le x\le 4$: $\dfrac{4-x}{1+x}\le 4-x$ because $4-x\ge 0$ and $1+x\ge 1$; equality only at $x=0$ and $x=4$. So the first-quadrant part is $\dfrac{4-x}{1+x}\le y\le 4-x$, $0\le x\le 4$ (a region between the line and an arc of a rectangular hyperbola).
originality_note: New: the region between the square |x| + |y| = 4 and the curve |x| + |y| + |xy| = 4, which factorises as (1+|x|)(1+|y|) = 5 (way 4, a hidden factorisation). Closest known: area inside |x| + |y| <= a outside a curve. Different because: the second boundary only becomes integrable after adding 1 and factorising, and both meet the square exactly at its four vertices on the axes.

concept_use.Area of a region defined by inequalities: The chain |x|+|y| <= 4 <= |x|+|y|+|xy| is turned into (4-x)/(1+x) <= y <= 4-x in the first quadrant.
concept_use.Area using symmetry of the region: Symmetry about both axes gives area = 4 times the first-quadrant part.
concept_use.Area of regions bounded by modulus curve: The outer boundary is the square |x| + |y| = 4, i.e. y = 4 - x in the first quadrant.

justification: Needs the factorisation idea plus symmetry and a log integral; numerical. Above the routine L2 region questions (2025-P2-Q2) because of the hidden factorisation; at the level of 2026-P2-Q18 (L3).
